successors.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
successors.text: the Medici grand duchy at Gian Gastone's death on 9 July 1737: Florence, Pisa, Livorno, Arezzo, Siena and the Maremma

ledger.x: 1115: the commune of Florence is established.
1494: Piero de' Medici gives Pisa and Livorno to Charles VIII and Pisa breaks away.
1532: the republic becomes the hereditary Duchy of Florence under Alessandro de' Medici.
1555: the exiled government of Siena holds Montalcino.
1555: Siena falls to Florence and Spain.
1557: Philip II hands Siena to Cosimo.
1557: Cosimo I of Florence receives the Sienese state as a hereditary fief.
1569: Cosimo I becomes Grand Duke of Tuscany.
1737: the Medici line ends with Gian Gastone.

wars.name: Florentine conquest of Pisa
wars.outcome: Maso degli Albizzi took Pisa on 9 October 1406 after a long siege and the city was annexed to Florence.

wars.name: Italian War of 1494-1495
wars.outcome: Piero de' Medici surrendered Sarzanello, Sarzana, Pietrasanta, Pisa and Livorno, was driven out on 8-9 November 1494 and the republic was restored; Charles VIII's occupation of Florence ended when he left for Rome in late November 1494.

wars.name: Pisan rebellion against Florence
wars.outcome: Pisa was 'de facto independent' from the French invasion of 1494 and was regained by Florence.

wars.name: Siege of Florence
wars.outcome: The Medici were restored after a protracted siege; Charles V created them hereditary rulers on 12 August 1530 and the republic became the Duchy of Florence in 1532.

wars.name: War of Siena
wars.outcome: The Sienese expelled the Spanish garrison in 1552 and allied with France; Piero Strozzi was beaten at Marciano in August 1554; Siena surrendered on 21 April 1555; Philip II ceded the territory to Cosimo in July 1557 and Tuscan troops annexed Montalcino in…
